title: Tokyo Japanese Language Schools That Provide Dormitories
summary: Of the Tokyo schools we cover, only some actually run dormitories. Here is what the two that publish details charge, and how a room gets allocated to you.
body_html:
"Dormitory available" appears on a lot of school pages and means several different things. Sometimes the school owns the buildings. Sometimes it introduces you to a share house operator. Sometimes it means a staff member will help you look.

Those are not the same offer, and only the first one gives you a room with a price attached before you arrive.

Of the Tokyo schools we cover, two publish real dormitory detail. Here is what they publish, and what the rest offer instead.

Akamonkai Japanese Language School: owns and manages its own

The school states that it owns and manages a large number of student dormitories, located near its campuses, at low cost and with simple initial procedures. [source:1]

The numbers it publishes:

  • Rent from 40,000 to 60,000 yen per month. [source:1]
  • Utilities charged separately by usage, with a guide figure of 5,000 to 10,000 yen per month. [source:1]
  • All within 40 minutes door to door of the campus. [source:1]
  • Around 30 buildings, at distances of 5 to 40 minutes from the campus. [source:1]
  • 2 dormitories reserved for women. [source:1]

Two details from the same page are worth more than the rent figure.

Bedding is not in the room. [source:1] A futon set — pillow, mattress and quilt — can be arranged if you order in advance, and you supply the covers yourself. [source:1] This is the kind of thing you discover at eleven at night on your first day if nobody tells you.

You state a preference, you do not choose. The school asks which dormitory you would like, and says plainly that you may be assigned one other than your preference. [source:1]

That second point is the honest part, and it is why the published rent range matters: if you can be placed anywhere in the range, budget for the top of it rather than the bottom.

Both share-house style rooms and apartment-style rooms are offered. [source:1]

The Sendagaya group: eight named dormitories, no published prices

The group that runs Sendagaya Japanese School, Sendagaya Japanese Institute and Sendagaya Language School lists its dormitories by name. [source:2]

Several carry conditions in the listing itself: some are men-only, one of those pairs the men-only rule with a meal-plan option, and another operates on meal tickets. [source:2]

What the group does not publish is price. There is no fee page on the site — not hidden behind a form, simply absent. So you cannot compare this option on cost without contacting them, and any figure you find quoted elsewhere is somebody's guess.

What they do publish, usefully, is the allocation process — and it is more specific than most schools manage.

How a dormitory actually gets assigned

The group sets out the sequence. [source:2] It is worth reading as a timeline rather than a list, because of where the money lands.

  • After you pass the school's admission screening, a staff member asks whether you want dormitory arrangement. [source:2]
  • If you do, you give first, second and third choices. [source:2]
  • About 2 months before enrolment, you are told which of your choices could actually be reserved. [source:2]
  • Cancelling after that point incurs a cancellation fee. [source:2]
  • You submit a residence pledge. [source:2]
  • After the Certificate of Eligibility is issued, the dormitory invoice comes together with the tuition invoice. [source:2]
  • Arrangement completes once the dormitory fee is paid. [source:2]

Read the order again. You learn which room you got about 2 months before you start. [source:2] You pay for it after your Certificate of Eligibility is issued. [source:2] And cancelling once allocated costs you. [source:2]

So the decision point is earlier than it feels. By the time you are choosing between a dormitory and renting your own place, you may already be past the moment where the dormitory was free to decline.

What the other schools offer instead

Not every school runs dormitories, and the alternatives are not inferior — they are different.

Kyoshin Language Academy's housing support is share house and homestay introduction rather than a dormitory it operates. [source:3] That means a third-party contract, third-party rules, and a price set by the operator rather than the school.

Among the others we cover, several publish no dormitory information at all. We are not going to list them as "no dormitory" on that basis — absence from a website is not a fact about a school, and the honest statement is that we could not verify one. Ask directly.

What to ask before you commit

  • Does the school own the building, or introduce you to someone who does? The answer determines who you complain to when the heating fails.
  • What is included? Akamonkai charges utilities separately on usage. [source:1] Assume separate unless told otherwise.
  • Is bedding there? [source:1] Ask about it specifically, for any school.
  • Can you decline after allocation, and what does that cost? [source:2]
  • When do you find out which room you got, and when do you pay? [source:2]
  • Men-only or women-only? Some of the Sendagaya dormitories carry that condition, named in the listing. [source:2]

If you are still weighing the dormitory against finding your own flat, the trade-offs run deeper than rent — see dormitory or your own apartment. Our Akamonkai profile and Kyoshin profile list what each school publishes.

Rents, availability and allocation procedures change, and are set by the schools rather than by us. The school pages are linked below and are the authority. We prepare and forward application documents; admission and all payments are between you and the school.

claims_without_sources: 千駄ヶ谷グループの寮の寮費 —— 集团站に価格の記載がない。「公表されていない」こと自体を書き、金額は一切推測していない。他サイトに出ている数字を引くこともしていない（出典が校方でない数字は本サイトでは使わない）。
寮を公表していない収録校を「寮なし」と列挙すること —— サイトに書いていないことは学校についての事実ではない。「確認できなかった」と書くに留めた。これは記事の網羅性を下げるが、未確認を断定に変えるほうが害が大きい。
寮と自己賃貸の費用比較 —— 赤門会の家賃は出典どおりだが、自己賃貸側の敷金・礼金・仲介手数料の相場は校方官網から取れない。本記事では比較していない（別記事でも金額は書いていない）。
各寮の最寄駅・徒歩分数 —— 寮名は公表されているが、個々の寮の所在地と駅からの距離は一覧ページに記載がないため書いていない。「校舎から5～40分」という赤門会の記述のみ出典付きで使った。
「約30棟」が現在も同数かどうか —— ページの記載時点の数であり、更新頻度は不明。記事中でも約（around）として引いている。
男子限定寮の「棟数」—— 一覧には男子限定の表示がある寮が複数あるが、学校は「男子限定は◯棟」という数え方を公表していない。当初こちらで数えて「two are men-only」と書いたが、それは出典の記述ではなく当方の集計なので「some」に改めた。英単語で綴れば闸门の数字検査を素通りしてしまう点も、書いてよい理由にはならない。
